item.title: 工信部：加快制造业中试建设 布局AI、量子科技等关键领域
item.description: 今日，工信部发布《关于进一步加快制造业中试平台体系化布局和高水平建设的通知》，旨在落实《制造业中试创新发展实施意见》，进一步推进制造业中试平台体系化布局，加强高水平中试平台建设。

item.title: Ultra-cold quantum sensors cut X-ray uncertainty, improving nuclear material assessments
item.description: To monitor the amount and type of nuclear material at power plants and weapons facilities, scientists look for a special signal—the unique pattern of gamma rays emitted by specific radioactive elements. However, some of these elements also emit X-rays in the same energy range as the gamma-ray emissions, masking the signal and making nuclear stockpiles harder to assess.

item.title: Unconventional quantum materials could dramatically boost the search for dark matter
item.description: For decades, physicists have searched for dark matter, the invisible substance thought to make up roughly 85% of all matter in the universe. Although its gravitational influence shapes galaxies and the large-scale structure of the cosmos, dark matter has never been directly detected. Now, an international team has identified a new class of quantum materials that could dramatically improve the search for some of the lightest and most elusive forms of dark matter.

item.title: 1,000 times faster operations bring reliable quantum computing a step closer
item.description: So far, quantum computers have been held back by their extreme sensitivity to errors and external disturbances. The longer a quantum operation takes, the greater the risk of computational errors.

item.title: Helium-3 lifts new quantum computing concept with faster tunneling rates
item.description: Helium—the lightest atom that can be laser-cooled and controlled—powers a new design for high-powered, stable quantum computers.

item.title: 四部门：推动科技保险高质量发展 在人工智能、集成电路、量子科技等领域开发专属产品
item.description: 昨日，科技部、金融监管总局、工业和信息化部、国家知识产权局联合印发《关于加快推动科技保险高质量发展 有力支撑高水平科技自立自强的若干意见》（以下简称《意见》），旨在健全重大技术攻关风险分散机制，构建覆盖科技创新全链条、全周期的科技保险政策体系。

item.title: 工信部召开务虚会 研究谋划“十五五”及开局之年工作：以综合整治“内卷式”竞争为重点
item.description: 2025年12月7日，工业和信息化部党组书记、部长李乐成主持召开务虚会，深入学习贯彻党的二十届四中全会精神，研究谋划“十五五”及开局之年工作思路和举措。部领导辛国斌、叶民、张云明、熊继军、柯吉欣、单忠德、谢远生、张建民、高东升、谢少锋、钟志红出席会议，结合分管领域工作逐一发言，交流学习体会，分析研判当前形势，提出意见建议。

item.title: 工信部筹建量子信息标准化技术委员会
item.description: 工信部官网发布消息，根据产业发展和行业管理需要，有关单位提出工业和信息化部量子信息标准化技术委员会的筹建方案。为进一步听取各方意见，现将筹建方案予以公示。

item.title: Mechanochromic tactile sensing
item.description: Nature Photonics, Published online: 28 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41566-026-01998-w Mechanochromic tactile sensing

item.title: Plasma mirror self-focusing boosts gamma-ray generation
item.description: Nature Photonics, Published online: 28 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41566-026-01993-1 One approach to generate high-energy X-rays and γ-rays is inverse Compton scattering, where a high-energy electron beam collides with an intense laser pulse. However, this process is notoriously difficult because the electron and laser beams must be precisely aligned in space and time. Now, a coated plasma mirror is shown to dramatically increase the efficiency and energy of the generation.

item.title: Time to embrace new platforms
item.description: Nature Photonics, Published online: 28 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41566-026-01996-y With silicon-based integrated photonics having reached commercial-level maturity, the research community is directing its efforts towards heterogeneous designs and alternative material platforms with new functionalities.

item.title: Tightly guided atoms could enable low-power quantum navigation when GPS fails
item.description: Within tiny halos of light clinging to a vanishingly thin wisp of optical fiber, scientist Jongmin Lee guides atoms like marbles through a narrow pipe. Rock the fiber and the atoms shift side by side; they just don't fall off. But don't be deceived by the seemingly delicate nature of his experiment. Lee is exploring how to measure motion precisely in rough-and-tumble environments.

item.title: New pulse-train method aims to improve precision in quantum control
item.description: Quantum technologies are poised to transform fields ranging from medicine and sensing to computing and communications by manipulating the energy states of atoms and molecules. These manipulations are achieved by controlling quantum states with laser pulses.

item.title: Bringing hidden optical imperfections to light
item.description: Tiny manufacturing imperfections in optical components normally go unnoticed. Yet they can alter light in surprisingly significant ways. An international research team led by TU Darmstadt has shown that such imperfections can affect not only polarization—the direction in which light oscillates—but also the spatial shape of a light beam.

item.title: Could quantum protocols make electronic voting more secure?
item.description: Electronic voting, the use of electronic systems to cast, record or count votes, could potentially simplify the process of electing new political leaders or other representatives. While some countries have already started using internet-connected devices or electronic voting machines at polling stations, the trustworthiness, security and anonymity of electronic voting systems are still widely debated.

item.title: A new game demonstrates quantum advantage with provable classical limits
item.description: For decades, physicists have worked to prove the strange predictions of quantum mechanics with real experiments. As quantum computers have grown more powerful, researchers have devised increasingly sophisticated ways to test whether these machines are truly harnessing quantum effects—but every method so far has run into limits.

item.title: Superfluid qubit could help scale up quantum computers
item.description: Superfluid helium could offer a new way to tackle one of the biggest challenges in scaling up quantum computers, say researchers from the University of Surrey. The research team has introduced a conceptual design for a new type of qubit that could be much less vulnerable to errors.

item.title: Entangled particles revive a 35-year-old test of the Standard Model
item.description: Physicists at the BESIII Collaboration have breathed new life into a decades-old test of one of the Standard Model's most important ideas, using a technique that had gone almost untouched by experimenters for 35 years.

item.title: Three quantum phases in chromium-based material hint at a spin-triplet superconductor
item.description: Superconductors are materials that conduct electricity without electrical resistance when cooled below a specific critical temperature. These materials have proved promising for the development of various technologies, including medical imaging instruments, particle accelerators, ultrasensitive detectors and quantum processors.

item.title: Quantum-optical spin glass could improve how AI remembers and learns
item.description: A new study has demonstrated that it is possible to make a network of atoms and photons that could improve how artificial intelligence stores and recalls memories. This network, called a quantum-optical spin glass, works as an associative memory, a form of AI that enables the recall of full memories from partial information—much like how humans can recognize a person's face in a blurred photograph.
